text: Accept the challenges so that you can feel the exhilaration of victory.
author: George S. Patton
title: General, U.S. Army

text: A good plan violently executed now is better than a perfect plan executed next week.
author: George S. Patton
title: General, U.S. Army

text: Never tell people how to do things. Tell them what to do and they will surprise you with their ingenuity.
author: George S. Patton
title: General, U.S. Army

text: Plans are worthless, but planning is everything.
author: Dwight D. Eisenhower
title: General of the Army
source: Remarks, National Defense Executive Reserve Conference, 1957

text: What counts is not necessarily the size of the dog in the fight; it's the size of the fight in the dog.
author: Dwight D. Eisenhower
title: General of the Army

text: I propose to fight it out on this line if it takes all summer.
author: Ulysses S. Grant
title: Lieutenant General, Union Army

text: In every battle there comes a time when both sides consider themselves beaten; then he who continues the attack wins.
author: Ulysses S. Grant
title: Lieutenant General, Union Army

text: The art of war is simple enough. Find out where your enemy is. Get at him as soon as you can. Strike him as hard as you can, and keep moving on.
author: Ulysses S. Grant
title: Lieutenant General, Union Army

text: Victory belongs to the most persevering.
author: Napoleon Bonaparte
title: Emperor of the French

text: Impossible is a word to be found only in the dictionary of fools.
author: Napoleon Bonaparte
title: Emperor of the French

text: The moral is to the physical as three to one.
author: Napoleon Bonaparte
title: Emperor of the French

text: If you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles.
author: Sun Tzu
title: General, State of Wu
source: The Art of War, ch. 3 (Giles translation)

text: The supreme art of war is to subdue the enemy without fighting.
author: Sun Tzu
title: General, State of Wu

text: Victorious warriors win first and then go to war, while defeated warriors go to war first and then seek to win.
author: Sun Tzu
title: General, State of Wu

text: The impediment to action advances action. What stands in the way becomes the way.
author: Marcus Aurelius
title: Roman Emperor

text: Waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. Be one.
author: Marcus Aurelius
title: Roman Emperor

text: Never give in, never give in, never, never, never, never.
author: Winston Churchill
title: Prime Minister

text: Uncommon valor was a common virtue.
author: Chester W. Nimitz
title: Fleet Admiral, U.S. Navy

text: I have not yet begun to fight!
author: John Paul Jones
title: Captain, Continental Navy

text: Perseverance and spirit have done wonders in all ages.
author: George Washington
title: Commander in Chief, Continental Army

text: It is better to offer no excuse than a bad one.
author: George Washington
title: Commander in Chief, Continental Army

text: Never take counsel of your fears.
author: Thomas J. "Stonewall" Jackson
title: Lieutenant General, Confederate Army

text: If you want to change the world, start off by making your bed.
author: William H. McRaven
title: Admiral, U.S. Navy

text: There are no secrets to success. It is the result of preparation, hard work, and learning from failure.
author: Colin Powell
title: General, U.S. Army

text: Come and take them.
author: Leonidas I
title: King of Sparta

text: Courage is fear holding on a minute longer.
author: George S. Patton
title: General, U.S. Army

text: Do everything you ask of those you command.
author: George S. Patton
title: General, U.S. Army

text: Pull the string, and it will follow wherever you wish. Push it, and it will go nowhere at all.
author: Dwight D. Eisenhower
title: General of the Army

text: We must all hang together, or most assuredly we shall all hang separately.
author: Benjamin Franklin
title: Founding Father
